about: Curriculum seed imported from the Learning Log artifact. Explore pointers are search prompts or named resources, never URLs.

topics.title: Arrays & the two-pointer pattern
topics.blurb: Learn to solve array problems in one pass by walking two indices toward or away from each other instead of nesting loops.
explore: Practice: "Two Sum II", "Container With Most Water"
Read about the two-pointer technique on a DSA reference site

topics.title: Sliding window
topics.blurb: A window that grows and shrinks over a sequence turns many O(n²) substring/subarray problems into O(n).
explore: Practice: "Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters"
Practice: "Minimum Window Substring"

topics.title: Hash maps for O(1) lookups
topics.blurb: Trade memory for speed: recognize when a problem is really asking "have I seen this before?"
explore: Practice: "Group Anagrams", "Subarray Sum Equals K"
Review hash collision handling (chaining vs. open addressing)

topics.title: Recursion & backtracking
topics.blurb: Build the mental model for exploring all choices and undoing them — the base for permutations, subsets, and puzzle solvers.
explore: Practice: "Subsets", "N-Queens", "Word Search"
Draw the recursion tree for one problem by hand before coding it

topics.title: Binary search beyond sorted arrays
topics.blurb: Binary search also works on answer spaces — searching for the smallest value that satisfies a condition.
explore: Practice: "Koko Eating Bananas", "Capacity To Ship Packages"
Write the invariant (lo/hi meaning) before coding the loop

topics.title: Trees: traversal & recursion
topics.blurb: Master pre/in/post-order and level-order traversal, then use them to solve height, diameter, and path-sum problems.
explore: Practice: "Diameter of Binary Tree", "Lowest Common Ancestor"
Implement traversal both recursively and iteratively with a stack

topics.title: Graphs: BFS & DFS
topics.blurb: Most graph problems reduce to a careful BFS or DFS — know when to use which and how to track visited state.
explore: Practice: "Number of Islands", "Course Schedule"
Review adjacency list vs. matrix trade-offs

topics.title: Dynamic programming: 1D
topics.blurb: Spot overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure; start with 1D DP (climbing stairs, house robber) before 2D.
explore: Practice: "Climbing Stairs", "House Robber", "Coin Change"
Write the recurrence relation in plain English first

topics.title: Dynamic programming: 2D & grids
topics.blurb: Extend DP to grids and strings — edit distance, longest common subsequence, unique paths.
explore: Practice: "Edit Distance", "Longest Common Subsequence"
Draw the DP table by hand for a small example

topics.title: Heaps & priority queues
topics.blurb: Learn when "give me the k smallest/largest" or "process by priority" signals a heap.
explore: Practice: "Kth Largest Element", "Merge k Sorted Lists"
Implement a min-heap from scratch once, by hand

topics.title: Big-O in practice
topics.blurb: Get fast at reading your own code's time and space complexity before you submit — interviewers watch for this.
explore: Rewrite 3 old solutions and label their Big-O
Compare an O(n log n) vs O(n) approach for one problem

topics.title: Union-Find (Disjoint Set)
topics.blurb: The go-to structure for "are these connected" and "group these into clusters" problems, with near-O(1) operations.
explore: Practice: "Number of Provinces", "Redundant Connection"
Implement union by rank + path compression

topics.title: What happens when you type a URL
topics.blurb: Walk the full path: DNS, TCP/TLS handshake, HTTP request, server processing, render — the classic warm-up question.
explore: Sketch the flow on paper, then check it against a reference diagram
Time yourself explaining it out loud in 3 minutes

topics.title: Load balancing basics
topics.blurb: Understand round robin, least connections, and consistent hashing — and why sticky sessions complicate things.
explore: Read how a reverse proxy like Nginx balances load
Sketch a 2-server setup with a load balancer in front

topics.title: Caching strategies
topics.blurb: Cache-aside, write-through, write-back — and the eviction policies (LRU, LFU) that decide what to keep.
explore: Implement an LRU cache from scratch (also a common DSA question)
Read about cache stampede and how TTL jitter helps

topics.title: Database indexing
topics.blurb: Learn how a B-tree index speeds up reads, why writes get slower, and when a full table scan is actually fine.
explore: Run EXPLAIN on a query in a database you use
Read about composite indexes and column order

topics.title: SQL vs NoSQL trade-offs
topics.blurb: Know when normalized relational data wins and when a document or key-value store fits better — concretely, not dogmatically.
explore: Pick one project idea and design its schema both ways
Read about eventual vs strong consistency

topics.title: API design: REST fundamentals
topics.blurb: Resource naming, status codes, idempotency, pagination — the details that separate clean APIs from messy ones.
explore: Review status codes 200 vs 201 vs 204 vs 409
Design pagination for a list endpoint you use often

topics.title: Message queues & async processing
topics.blurb: Understand why you'd put a queue between two services, and the at-least-once vs exactly-once delivery trade-off.
explore: Read the basic architecture of a queue like RabbitMQ or SQS
Sketch a system where a queue decouples a slow email job

topics.title: Horizontal vs vertical scaling
topics.blurb: Know the limits of "just get a bigger server" and what statelessness buys you when you scale out.
explore: List what must be true for a service to scale horizontally
Read about sharding a database by key

topics.title: Rate limiting
topics.blurb: Token bucket vs sliding window vs fixed window — how APIs protect themselves from abuse and overload.
explore: Implement a token bucket rate limiter from scratch
Read how a CDN or API gateway applies rate limits

topics.title: Design a URL shortener
topics.blurb: A classic first system design problem — combines hashing, database schema, and read-heavy scaling in one exercise.
explore: Design it end to end on paper: API, schema, ID generation
Compare base62 encoding vs random ID generation

topics.title: CAP theorem, in practice
topics.blurb: Consistency, availability, partition tolerance — understand it through real examples instead of memorizing the triangle.
explore: Match 3 databases you know to where they sit on CAP
Read a concrete example of a network partition trade-off

topics.title: Observability: logs, metrics, traces
topics.blurb: You can't fix what you can't see — learn the three pillars and when to reach for each one.
explore: Add structured logging to one small project
Read about the difference between a metric and a trace

topics.title: How the event loop actually works
topics.blurb: Microtasks vs macrotasks, call stack, callback queue — the mental model behind every async bug you'll debug.
explore: Predict the output of a script mixing setTimeout and Promises, then run it
Read about the difference between microtask and macrotask queues

topics.title: Closures, from first principles
topics.blurb: Understand exactly what a closure captures and why — this explains half the "weird" bugs in loops and callbacks.
explore: Write a counter factory function from scratch, no libraries
Explain why `var` in a loop behaves differently from `let`

topics.title: Memory: stack vs heap
topics.blurb: Know what lives where, what gets garbage collected, and why passing objects behaves differently from passing primitives.
explore: Trace through a function call by hand, noting stack frames
Read how your language's garbage collector decides what to free

topics.title: Concurrency primitives
topics.blurb: Threads, locks, mutexes, and race conditions — the vocabulary you need before touching concurrent code at work.
explore: Write a small program with a deliberate race condition, then fix it
Read about deadlock and the four conditions that cause it

topics.title: Type systems: static vs dynamic
topics.blurb: Understand what a type checker actually buys you, and where dynamic typing genuinely moves faster.
explore: Add types to one untyped function and see what bugs surface
Read about structural vs nominal typing

topics.title: Error handling patterns
topics.blurb: Exceptions vs. return-value errors vs. Result/Option types — and why "just catch everything" is a trap.
explore: Refactor one function to handle errors explicitly instead of catching broadly
Read how a language you don't use handles errors (contrast is clarifying)

topics.title: How a compiler or interpreter runs your code
topics.blurb: Lexing, parsing, and execution — a rough mental model of the pipeline between your source file and a running program.
explore: Read a short intro to how your main language is parsed and executed
Try writing a tiny expression evaluator (tokenize → parse → evaluate)

topics.title: Dependency injection & testable code
topics.blurb: Learn why passing dependencies in (instead of hardcoding them) makes code testable and swappable.
explore: Refactor one function to accept its dependency as a parameter
Write a unit test that swaps in a fake dependency

topics.title: Immutability and why it matters
topics.blurb: Understand how immutable data avoids a whole class of bugs in shared state and concurrent code.
explore: Rewrite a mutating function to return a new value instead
Read how your framework of choice encourages (or fights) immutability

topics.title: Reading a stack trace properly
topics.blurb: A skill nobody teaches directly — learn to read a trace top to bottom and separate your code from library noise.
explore: Take a real stack trace from a past bug and annotate each frame
Practice reproducing an error deliberately, just to read its trace

topics.title: Git internals: commits, branches, and HEAD
topics.blurb: Understand what a commit actually is (a snapshot + parent pointer) so branching and rebasing stop feeling magical.
explore: Run `git log --graph` on a real repo and trace the history by hand
Practice an interactive rebase on a throwaway branch

topics.title: HTTP, headers, and status codes
topics.blurb: Go past "200 means OK" — understand headers, caching directives, and the request/response lifecycle.
explore: Inspect the network tab on a site you use and read every header
Read the difference between 401 and 403

topics.title: TCP vs UDP
topics.blurb: Reliable, ordered delivery vs fast, connectionless — know which trade-off fits which kind of application.
explore: List 3 apps that use TCP and 3 that use UDP, and explain why
Read about the TCP three-way handshake

topics.title: Processes vs threads
topics.blurb: Understand isolation, shared memory, and context-switch cost — the basis for every concurrency decision above this.
explore: Read how your OS scheduler switches between processes
Compare memory isolation: process vs thread

topics.title: How databases guarantee transactions (ACID)
topics.blurb: Atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability — what actually breaks when one of these is relaxed.
explore: Read about isolation levels (read committed vs serializable)
Find a real example of a lost-update bug and how ACID prevents it

topics.title: Big-endian, hex, and how data is actually stored
topics.blurb: A low-level topic worth an hour — demystifies debugging binary data and reading memory dumps.
explore: Convert a few numbers between decimal, hex, and binary by hand
Read about endianness and why it matters across systems

topics.title: DNS, step by step
topics.blurb: Recursive resolvers, root servers, TLDs, and caching — what actually happens before a single byte of your request is sent.
explore: Run `dig` or `nslookup` on a domain and read the full chain
Read about DNS TTL and why changes take time to propagate

topics.title: Writing a good README and commit message
topics.blurb: An underrated skill — clear commits and docs are what make you easy to work with on a team.
explore: Rewrite your last 5 commit messages to follow a clear convention
Read a well-written README from a popular open-source project

topics.title: Testing pyramid: unit, integration, e2e
topics.blurb: Understand why you want many fast unit tests and few slow end-to-end tests, not the reverse.
explore: Write one unit test and one integration test for the same feature
Read about the cost/confidence trade-off at each testing layer

topics.title: Reading someone else's codebase
topics.blurb: A concrete skill: start from the entry point, follow one request end to end, and resist reading everything at once.
explore: Pick an open-source repo and trace one feature from entry to output
Time-box it to 45 minutes and write down what you learned

topics.title: Read one real production postmortem
topics.blurb: Public postmortems are some of the best engineering writing there is — see how a real team diagnosed and fixed a real outage, under pressure, with incomplete information.
explore: Search an engineering blog's postmortem or incident report (Cloudflare, GitHub, Slack, and Vercel all publish theirs)
Write 3 sentences: what broke, what caught it, what they changed after

topics.title: Spend 20 minutes on what's trending in software
topics.blurb: Staying current isn't a side effect of working — it's a habit. Twenty focused minutes a day compounds fast.
explore: Browse Hacker News or GitHub Trending for 20 minutes, no goal beyond noticing
Pick one tool or story and write 2 sentences on why it matters

topics.title: Situational: a production error spike
topics.blurb: A scenario, not a lecture. Your API's error rate just tripled in production, right now. Think through your first five actions before you touch any code.
explore: Write your triage checklist: what do you check first, second, third?
Compare it against a real incident-response runbook afterward

topics.title: Read a real system-design write-up
topics.blurb: Company engineering blogs regularly publish exactly how they built something at scale — a free architecture review from people who've actually done it.
explore: Search "[company] engineering blog architecture" for Netflix, Uber, Airbnb, Shopify, or Discord
Note one design decision you wouldn't have made yourself, and why they did

topics.title: Situational: a teammate's PR broke the build
topics.blurb: A scenario for judgment, not syntax. A coworker's merged PR just broke the build on main, and they're offline for the day. Walk through exactly what you'd do, in order.
explore: Write out your exact next 3 actions, in order
Think through how you'd flag it to the team without it sounding like blame

topics.title: Read about a real security incident
topics.blurb: Understanding how real breaches actually happened builds the instinct to spot risky code before it ships — most root causes are surprisingly ordinary.
explore: Search for a post-incident security report or an OWASP case study
Write the root cause in one plain sentence

topics.title: Situational: your estimate was wrong
topics.blurb: A scenario in planning judgment. A feature you estimated at 2 days is now on day 5, and the deadline is tomorrow. Think through what you'd do, and what you'd actually say in standup.
explore: Write the exact words you'd use to flag it early, next time
Read how experienced engineers pad and communicate estimates

topics.title: Follow one experienced engineer's writing
topics.blurb: A single well-chosen blog beats a hundred random tutorials — find a writer whose judgment you trust and read through their backlog.
explore: Search for a senior engineer's personal blog (Julia Evans and Martin Fowler are two well-known starting points)
Read one full post and note one idea you'd never considered before

topics.title: Situational: reviewing risky code
topics.blurb: A scenario in code review. A PR touches your service's payment logic, and the tests look thin. Decide exactly what you'd ask for before approving it.
explore: List 3 specific questions or changes you'd request on the PR
Search for a public code-review style guide and compare it to your list

topics.title: Read a "why we rewrote it" story
topics.blurb: Rewrite postmortems are unusually honest about what went wrong the first time — a fast way to learn hard lessons secondhand instead of the hard way.
explore: Search "why we rewrote" or "we migrated from" plus an engineering blog
Note what actually forced the decision, not just what changed

topics.title: Situational: an ambiguous ticket
topics.blurb: A scenario in requirements. You're handed a ticket that just says "make search better," with no other detail. Think through every question you'd ask before writing a line of code.
explore: Write 5 clarifying questions you'd actually ask
Think through how a senior engineer might scope the same vague ticket

topics.title: Learn one new tool, shallowly on purpose
topics.blurb: You don't need to master everything in your field — you need to know what exists and roughly when you'd reach for it.
explore: Pick one unfamiliar tool and read its own "why we built this" page
Write one sentence: what problem does it solve, and would you reach for it?
